diffuseColor.comment: When using metallic workflow this is interpreted as albedo.
diffuseColor.name: diffuseColor

displacement.comment: Displacement in the direction of the normal.
displacement.name: displacement

ior.comment: Index of Refraction to be used for translucent objects and objects with specular components, including the clearcoat if clearcoat > 0.
ior.name: ior

metallic.comment: Use 1 for metallic surfaces and 0 for non-metallic.  If metallic is 1, then both F0 (reflectivity at 0 degree incidence) and edge F90 reflectivity will simply be the Albedo.  If metallic is 0, then Albedo is ignored in the calculation of F0 and F90; F0 is derived from ior via ( (1-ior)/(1+ior) )^2 and F90 is white. In between, we interpolate.
metallic.name: metallic

opacity.comment: When opacity is 1.0 then the geometry is fully opaque, if it is smaller than 1.0 then the geometry is translucent, when it is 0 the geometry is transparent. Note that even a fully transparent object still receives lighting as, for example, perfectly clear glass still has a specular response.
opacity.name: opacity

opacityThreshold.comment: The opacityThreshold input is useful for creating geometric cut-outs based on the opacity input. A value of 0.0 indicates that no masking is applied to the opacity input, while a value greater than 0.0 indicates that rendering of the surface is limited to the areas where the opacity is greater or equal to that value.
opacityThreshold.name: opacityThreshold

roughness.comment: Roughness for the specular lobe. The value ranges from 0 to 1, which goes from a perfectly specular surface at 0.0 to maximum roughness of the specular lobe.
roughness.name: roughness

specularColor.comment: Specular color to be used. This is the color at 0 incidence. Edge color is assumed white. Transition between the two colors according to Schlick fresnel approximation.
specularColor.name: specularColor

useSpecularWorkflow.comment: This node can fundamentally operate in two modes : Specular workflow where you provide a texture/value to the 'specularColor' input. Or, Metallic workflow where you provide a texture/value to the 'metallic' input.
useSpecularWorkflow.name: useSpecularWorkflow
